tools.description:

- **/*.{js,ts} to match all js/ts files in the workspace.
- src/** to match all files under the top-level src folder.
- **/foo/**/*.js to match all js files under any foo folder in the workspace.

In a multi-root workspace, you can scope the search to a specific workspace folder by using the absolute path to the folder as the query, e.g. /path/to/folder/**/*.ts.

For example, use 'function|method|procedure' to look for all of those words at once. Use includePattern to search within files matching a specific pattern, or in a specific file, using a relative path. Use 'includeIgnoredFiles' to include files normally ignored by .gitignore, other ignore files, and `files.exclude` and `search.exclude` settings. Warning: using this may cause the search to be slower, only set it when you want to search in ignored folders like node_modules or build outputs. Use this tool when you want to see an overview of a particular file, instead of using read_file many times to look for code within a file.

In a multi-root workspace, you can scope the search to a specific workspace folder by using the absolute path to the folder as the includePattern, e.g. /path/to/folder.

tools.description:
This tool allows you to execute Windows PowerShell 5.1 commands in a persistent terminal session, preserving environment variables, working directory, and other context across multiple commands.

Command Execution:
- Use semicolons ; to chain commands on one line, NEVER use && even when asked explicitly
- Prefer pipelines | for object-based data flow
- Never create a sub-shell (eg. powershell -c "command") unless explicitly asked

Directory Management:
- Prefer relative paths when navigating directories, only use absolute when the path is far away or the current cwd is not expected
- By default (mode=sync), shell and cwd are reused by subsequent sync commands
- Use $PWD or Get-Location for current directory
- Use Push-Location/Pop-Location for directory stack

Program Execution:
- Supports .NET, Python, Node.js, and other executables
- Install modules via Install-Module, Install-Package
- Use Get-Command to verify cmdlet/function availability

Async Mode:
- For long-running tasks (e.g., servers), use mode=async
- Returns a terminal ID for checking status and runtime later
- Use send_to_terminal to send commands to a persistent terminal session (async mode)
- Use Start-Job for background PowerShell jobs

Output Management:
- Output is automatically truncated if longer than 60KB to prevent context overflow
- Use Select-Object, Where-Object, Format-Table to filter output
- Use -First/-Last parameters to limit results
- For pager commands, add | Out-String or | Format-List

Best Practices:
- Use proper cmdlet names instead of aliases in scripts
- Quote paths with spaces: "C:\Path With Spaces"
- Prefer PowerShell cmdlets over external commands when available
- Prefer idiomatic PowerShell like Get-ChildItem instead of dir or ls for file listings
- Use Test-Path to check file/directory existence
- Be specific with Select-Object properties to avoid excessive output
- Avoid printing credentials unless absolutely required
- NEVER run Start-Sleep or similar wait commands. Use get_terminal_output to check output before then

Execution mode:
- mode='sync': wait for completion up to timeout; if still running, return with a terminal ID.
- mode='async': wait for an initial idle/output signal, then return with terminal output snapshot and ID.

Use get_terminal_output to check on async terminal output. Do NOT poll or sleep to wait for completion.

command.description: The command to run in the terminal.

explanation.description: A one-sentence description of what the command does. This will be shown to the user before the command is run.

goal.description: A short description of the goal or purpose of the command (e.g., "Install dependencies", "Start development server").

fields:
  - name: id
    type: string
    description: "Unique ticket identifier (e.g. TASK-009, FEATURE-001). Immutable after creation."

  - name: type
    type: enum
    description: "Ticket type key. Determines workflow, file prefix, and folder name."
    values: [task, feature, epic, dev_story, bug, resource_req, workitem,
             ba_subtask_analysis, ba_subtask_design,
             sa_subtask_analysis, sa_subtask_design,
             ux_subtask_analysis, ux_subtask_design,
             design, development,
             unittest, codereview, testcase, testexec, devops, bug_subtask, question]

  - name: title
    type: string
    description: "Short, descriptive summary of the ticket. Immutable after creation."

  - name: status
    type: string
    description: "Current lifecycle status. Valid values depend on ticket type (see ticket_types)."

  - name: priority
    type: enum
    description: "Urgency and importance of the ticket."
    values: [Low, Medium, High, Critical]

  - name: assignee
    type: string
    description: "Agent or role responsible for current status activities."

  - name: reporter
    type: string
    description: "Agent or role who created the ticket."

  - name: parent
    type: string
    description: >-
      Parent ticket ID. Derived from physical folder nesting — NOT stored in ticket.md
      frontmatter. Persisted only in .config/.index.csv for fast lookup. Folder location
      is the authoritative source of parentage.

  - name: addressed_to
    type: string
    description: "Target agent or role for Question tickets."

  - name: epic
    type: string
    description: "Epic ticket ID this Dev Story belongs to (logical grouping)."

  - name: feature_request
    type: string
    description: "Feature Request ID this ticket implements or belongs to."

  - name: component
    type: string
    description: "Functional component or module the ticket relates to."

  - name: labels
    type: list
    description: "Free-form classification tags (e.g. backend, ui, security)."

  - name: sprint
    type: string
    description: "Sprint name or identifier this ticket is scheduled for."

  - name: story_points
    type: integer
    description: "Effort estimate in Fibonacci points (Developer Stories only)."

  - name: estimated_hours
    type: float
    description: "Estimated hours to complete (Sub-Tasks only)."

  - name: time_spent_hours
    type: float
    description: "Actual hours spent (Sub-Tasks only)."

  - name: due_date
    type: date
    description: "Target completion date (ISO 8601)."

  - name: affected_version
    type: string
    description: "Product version where the bug was observed (Bug tickets only)."

  - name: fix_version
    type: string
    description: "Product version where the fix will be delivered."

  - name: release_notes
    type: string
    description: "Human-readable description of what changed (Developer Story only)."

  - name: resolution
    type: enum
    description: "How the ticket was resolved."
    values: [Done, Rejected, Canceled, Duplicated, Fixed, WontFix]

  - name: created
    type: date
    description: "Date ticket was created (ISO 8601). Immutable."

  - name: updated
    type: date
    description: "Date ticket was last modified (ISO 8601)."

# Tracker System Configuration

**Version**: 3.4  
**Created**: 2026-01-04  
**Updated**: 2026-02-23  
**Purpose**: System-wide configuration for file-based issue tracking

---

## ID Counters

ID counters are stored in a dedicated structured file:

```yaml
id_counters_file: ".ept/tracker/.config/.id-counters.yaml"
```

**Usage**: Read `.config/.id-counters.yaml` to get current counters. After creating a ticket/link, increment the relevant counter in `.config/.id-counters.yaml`. Zero-pad to 3 digits for tickets (e.g., 001, 042, 123), 5 digits for links (e.g., LINK-00001).

---

## Link Management

```yaml
link_storage:
  file: ".config/.link-index.csv"
  format: "csv"
  status: "active"        # active | migrating | legacy
  location: ".ept/tracker/.config/"    # Config subfolder of tracker
  
# link_types and link_roles_mapping: see .config/.workflow.yaml (link_types section)

link_consistency:
  validation_enabled: true
  validation_frequency: "weekly"
  auto_repair: true       # Repair orphaned/broken links
  
link_operations:
  atomic: true            # All operations are atomic
  locking: true           # File locking during writes
  backup_on_update: false # Backup before each update (set true for safety)
```

**Usage**:

- All relationship links stored in `.ept/tracker/.config/.link-index.csv`
- Update `link_id_counter` (in id_counters section) after creating each link
- Migration from links.md files completed in v2.4 (TASK-031/032)

---

## Folder Structure

```yaml
folder_structure:
  root_level:
    - .config/             # Configuration subfolder (NEW in v3.4)
    - .instructions/       # Ticket type handling algorithms (YAML)
    - README.md            # User guide
    - project_qa.md        # Q&A knowledge base
    - FEATURE-XXX/         # Feature Request folders
    - EPIC-XXX/            # Epic folders (independent, linked to Features)
    - TASK-XXX/            # Task folders (general-purpose)
    - BUG-XXX/             # Production/UAT Bug folders
    - RESOURCE-REQ-XXX/    # Resource/Agent Request folders
  
  config_folder_contents:
    - .link-index.csv      # Centralized link storage
    - .index.csv           # Ticket index
    - .tracker-config.md   # This configuration file
    - .id-counters.yaml    # ID counters (structured, separate file)
    - .workflow.yaml       # Workflow specification (fields, ticket types, link types)
  
  ticket_folder_contents:
    - ticket.md            # ALL ticket types — single consistent content filename
    - comments/            # One file per comment: yyyymmdd-hhmmss-author.md
  
  task_children:
    - WORK-XXX/           # Work Item sub-tasks (for Task decomposition)
    - QUESTION-XXX/       # Question sub-task (can be child of any task/sub-task)
  
  feature_request_children:
    - BA-ANA-XXX/         # BA Analysis sub-tasks (ANALYSIS stage)
    - BA-DES-XXX/         # BA Design sub-tasks (DESIGN stage)
    - SA-ANA-XXX/         # SA Analysis sub-tasks (ANALYSIS stage)
    - SA-DES-XXX/         # SA Design sub-tasks (DESIGN stage)
    - UX-ANA-XXX/         # UX Analysis sub-tasks (ANALYSIS stage)
    - UX-DES-XXX/         # UX Design sub-tasks (DESIGN stage)
    - DEV-STORY-XXX/      # Developer Stories (nested in Feature, not Epic)

    - DEV-XXX/            # Development sub-task

**Key Principle**: Developer Stories are physically nested under Feature Requests, NOT under Epics. Epics live at root level and are linked to Stories via "Epic Link" field.

## Link Types

### Hierarchical Links (via frontmatter fields)

```yaml
hierarchical_relationships:
  - type: "parent"
    description: "Parent ticket ID (folder location for physical nesting)"
    examples:
      - "Developer Story → parent: FEATURE-001 (physically nested in Feature folder)"
      - "Sub-Task → parent: DEV-STORY-001 or parent: DEV-001 (nested)"
      - "Question → parent: <any-ticket-id> (nested as child)"
  
  - type: "epic"
    description: "Epic Link field (logical grouping, NOT physical nesting)"
    examples:
      - "Developer Story → epic: EPIC-001 (for organizational purposes)"
  
  - type: "feature_request"
    description: "Feature Request this ticket implements/belongs to"
    examples:
      - "Epic → feature_request: FEATURE-001 (linked)"
      - "Developer Story → feature_request: FEATURE-001 (same as parent)"
```

> **Note**: Relationship link type definitions (types, roles, descriptions, usage) are maintained in `.workflow.yaml` (`link_types` section).

### Link Storage Schema

```yaml
link_index_csv_schema:
  columns:
    - link_id: "Unique identifier (LINK-XXXXX)"
    - source_ticket: "Source ticket ID"
    - target_ticket: "Target ticket ID"
    - link_type: "Standardized link type (see relationship_link_types)"
    - source_role: "Role from source perspective"
    - target_role: "Role from target perspective"
    - created: "ISO 8601 timestamp"
    - created_by: "Agent name"
    - comment: "Optional description"
  
  example_row:
    "LINK-00001,FEATURE-001,EPIC-001,FeatureContains,Feature Contains,Is Contained In Feature,2026-01-18T20:00:00Z,architect,Initial Feature-Epic link"
```

### Link Consistency and Validation

With centralized storage in `.link-index.csv`, consistency is inherently maintained:

```yaml
link_consistency:
  enforcement: "strict"
  single_source_of_truth: true  # No synchronization needed between files
  atomic_operations: true       # All link CRUD operations are atomic
  foreign_key_validation: true  # All referenced tickets must exist
  uniqueness_constraint: true   # No duplicate links (same source, target, type)
  
  link_creation:
    steps:
      - "1. Validate both tickets exist"
      - "2. Check link_type is valid"
      - "3. Check for duplicate links"
      - "4. Generate next link_id from counter"
      - "5. Append row to .config/.link-index.csv"
      - "6. Update link counter in .config/.id-counters.yaml"
      - "7. Update timestamps on both tickets"
    rollback_on_failure: true
    
  link_deletion:
    steps:
      - "1. Find link by link_id in .config/.link-index.csv"
      - "2. Remove row from CSV (rewrite file)"
      - "3. Update timestamps on both tickets"
      - "4. Add comments if deletion is significant"
    atomic: true
    
  link_update:
    process: "Delete old link + Create new link (preserving created timestamp)"
    atomic: true
    comment: "Add comment explaining change"
  
  validation:
    frequency: "Weekly (recommended)"
    checks:
      - "All source_ticket and target_ticket exist"
      - "No duplicate link_ids"
      - "No duplicate links (same source, target, type)"
      - "All link_types are valid"
      - "Orphaned links detected and reported"
    
  auto_repair:
    enabled: true
    safe_operations:
      - "Remove links where both tickets don't exist (orphaned)"
      - "Fix malformed link_ids"
      - "Remove duplicate links"
    manual_review_required:
      - "Links with invalid link_type"
      - "Links where one ticket exists but other doesn't"
      - "Circular dependencies"
```

tools.name: file_search
tools.description:
Search for files in the workspace by glob pattern. This only returns the paths of matching files. Use this tool when you know the exact filename pattern of the files you're searching for. Glob patterns match from the root of the workspace folder. Examples:
- **/*.{js,ts} to match all js/ts files in the workspace.
- src/** to match all files under the top-level src folder.
- **/foo/**/*.js to match all js files under any foo folder in the workspace.

In a multi-root workspace, you can scope the search to a specific workspace folder by using the absolute path to the folder as the query, e.g. /path/to/folder/**/*.ts.

query.description: Search for files with names or paths matching this glob pattern. Can also be an absolute path to a workspace folder to scope the search in a multi-root workspace.

maxResults.description: The maximum number of results to return. Do not use this unless necessary, it can slow things down. By default, only some matches are returned. If you use this and don't see what you're looking for, you can try again with a more specific query or a larger maxResults.

tools.name: grep_search
tools.description:
Do a fast text search in the workspace. Use this tool when you want to search with an exact string or regex. If you are not sure what words will appear in the workspace, prefer using regex patterns with alternation (|) or character classes to search for multiple potential words at once instead of making separate searches. For example, use 'function|method|procedure' to look for all of those words at once. Use includePattern to search within files matching a specific pattern, or in a specific file, using a relative path. Use 'includeIgnoredFiles' to include files normally ignored by .gitignore, other ignore files, and `files.exclude` and `search.exclude` settings. Warning: using this may cause the search to be slower, only set it when you want to search in ignored folders like node_modules or build outputs. Use this tool when you want to see an overview of a particular file, instead of using read_file many times to look for code within a file.

In a multi-root workspace, you can scope the search to a specific workspace folder by using the absolute path to the folder as the includePattern, e.g. /path/to/folder.

query.description: The pattern to search for in files in the workspace. Use regex with alternation (e.g., 'word1|word2|word3') or character classes to find multiple potential words in a single search. Be sure to set the isRegexp property properly to declare whether it's a regex or plain text pattern. Is case-insensitive.

isRegexp.description: Whether the pattern is a regex.

includePattern.description: Search files matching this glob pattern. Will be applied to the relative path of files within the workspace. To search recursively inside a folder, use a proper glob pattern like "src/folder/**". Do not use | in includePattern. Can also be an absolute path to a workspace folder to scope the search in a multi-root workspace.

maxResults.description: The maximum number of results to return. Do not use this unless necessary, it can slow things down. By default, only some matches are returned. If you use this and don't see what you're looking for, you can try again with a more specific query or a larger maxResults.

includeIgnoredFiles.description: Whether to include files that would normally be ignored according to .gitignore, other ignore files and `files.exclude` and `search.exclude` settings. Warning: using this may cause the search to be slower. Only set it when you want to search in ignored folders like node_modules or build outputs.

      - target_statuses: [Resolved]
        dod_criteria:
          - "Studied related documentation from the `.ept/docs/document_index.md`"
          - Critical thinking applied
          - All required questions asked and answered
          - All Developer Stories created and nested under FEATURE-XXX
          - All Developer Stories assigned to appropriate developers
          - Epic links set in all Developer Stories
          - All links registered in the link index (via the CLI)
          - ALL linked Developer Stories reach Closed status (automatic)

  Resolved:
    instructions:
      - "Review answers from linked QUESTION tickets: Query Question links on this ticket via the CLI. For each linked QUESTION ticket found: retrieve it via the CLI, read its Answer section and comments, and incorporate findings/decisions into current work."
      - Automatically entered when ALL linked Developer Stories reach Closed status.
      - IF blocker link exists AND blocker resolved THEN remove the blocking link via the CLI.
      - IF resolution not set THEN set Done/Canceled/Duplicated.
      - THEN move to Closed when ready to archive.
    transition_dods:
      - target_statuses: [Closed]
        dod_criteria: []

  Closed:
    instructions:
      - Archive only; no edits.
    transition_dods: []

  Blocked:
    instructions:
      - Confirm blocker and prior status are documented as a comment on this ticket (include blocker ID and prior status).
      - Verify blocking link exists on this ticket via the CLI.
      - Do not create new blocker links in this status; they must be created when the block is identified.
      - "IF blocking link missing THEN create QUESTION-XXX addressed_to appropriate role, add a Blocks link from the question to this ticket via the CLI, and remain Blocked."
      - "Query blocking links on this ticket via the CLI. For each blocker found: IF blocker status IN `Closed`, `Done`, `Canceled`, `Rejected`, `Duplicated` THEN remove the blocking link via the CLI and return to prior status; IF blocker still active AND blocker priority lower than this ticket priority THEN raise blocker priority to match."
      - IF all blocking links removed THEN return to prior status documented in comments.
    transition_dods: []

# ─────────────────────────────────────────
# FIELDS
# ─────────────────────────────────────────
fields:
  - name: id
    type: string
    description: "Unique ticket identifier (e.g. TASK-009, FEATURE-001). Immutable after creation."

  - name: type
    type: enum
    description: "Ticket type key. Determines workflow, file prefix, and folder name."
    values: [task, feature, epic, dev_story, bug, resource_req, workitem,
             ba_subtask_analysis, ba_subtask_design,
             sa_subtask_analysis, sa_subtask_design,
             ux_subtask_analysis, ux_subtask_design,
             design, development,
             unittest, codereview, testcase, testexec, devops, bug_subtask, question]

  - name: title
    type: string
    description: "Short, descriptive summary of the ticket. Immutable after creation."

  - name: status
    type: string
    description: "Current lifecycle status. Valid values depend on ticket type (see ticket_types)."

  - name: priority
    type: enum
    description: "Urgency and importance of the ticket."
    values: [Low, Medium, High, Critical]

  - name: assignee
    type: string
    description: "Agent or role responsible for current status activities."

  - name: reporter
    type: string
    description: "Agent or role who created the ticket."

  - name: parent
    type: string
    description: >-
      Parent ticket ID. Derived from physical folder nesting — NOT stored in ticket.md
      frontmatter. Persisted only in .config/.index.csv for fast lookup. Folder location
      is the authoritative source of parentage.

  - name: addressed_to
    type: string
    description: "Target agent or role for Question tickets."

  - name: epic
    type: string
    description: "Epic ticket ID this Dev Story belongs to (logical grouping)."

  - name: feature_request
    type: string
    description: "Feature Request ID this ticket implements or belongs to."

  - name: component
    type: string
    description: "Functional component or module the ticket relates to."

  - name: labels
    type: list
    description: "Free-form classification tags (e.g. backend, ui, security)."

  - name: sprint
    type: string
    description: "Sprint name or identifier this ticket is scheduled for."

  - name: story_points
    type: integer
    description: "Effort estimate in Fibonacci points (Developer Stories only)."

  - name: estimated_hours
    type: float
    description: "Estimated hours to complete (Sub-Tasks only)."

  - name: time_spent_hours
    type: float
    description: "Actual hours spent (Sub-Tasks only)."

  - name: due_date
    type: date
    description: "Target completion date (ISO 8601)."

  - name: affected_version
    type: string
    description: "Product version where the bug was observed (Bug tickets only)."

  - name: fix_version
    type: string
    description: "Product version where the fix will be delivered."

  - name: release_notes
    type: string
    description: "Human-readable description of what changed (Developer Story only)."

  - name: resolution
    type: enum
    description: "How the ticket was resolved."
    values: [Done, Rejected, Canceled, Duplicated, Fixed, WontFix]

  - name: created
    type: date
    description: "Date ticket was created (ISO 8601). Immutable."

  - name: updated
    type: date
    description: "Date ticket was last modified (ISO 8601)."


# ─────────────────────────────────────────
# TICKET TYPES
# ─────────────────────────────────────────
ticket_types:
  - $ref: tickets/task.yaml
  - $ref: tickets/feature.yaml

  - $ref: tickets/bug_subtask.yaml
  - $ref: tickets/question.yaml
# ─────────────────────────────────────────
# LINK TYPES
# ─────────────────────────────────────────
link_types:

  - type: Blocks
    source_role: "Blocks"
    target_role: "Is Blocked By"
    description: "Blocking relationship. Source ticket prevents progress on target ticket."
    usage: "Any ticket can block any other ticket."

  - type: DependsOn
    source_role: "Depends On"
    target_role: "Is Dependency For"
    description: "Dependency relationship. Source must wait for target to complete first."
    usage: "Ticket requires another ticket to be completed before it can proceed."

  - type: RelatesTo
    source_role: "Relates To"
    target_role: "Relates To"
    description: "General symmetric relationship with no ordering implication."
    usage: "Any loosely related tickets that share context."

  - type: Contains
    source_role: "Contains"
    target_role: "Contained In"
    description: "Containment/parent-child relationship mirroring folder structure."
    usage: "Feature Request → Developer Story; Developer Story → Sub-Task."

  - type: EpicLink
    source_role: "Epic Link"
    target_role: "Epic Link"
    description: "Symmetric association between an Epic and a Developer Story."
    usage: "Links a Developer Story to its organizing Epic (logical grouping)."

  - type: FeatureContains
    source_role: "Feature Contains"
    target_role: "Is Contained In Feature"
    description: "Feature-to-Epic organizational relationship."
    usage: "Feature Request ↔ Epic (many-to-many, bidirectional)."

  - type: BugFeature
    source_role: "Comes From"
    target_role: "Goes To"
    description: "A bug that requires a new Feature Request to address it properly."
    usage: "Bug → Feature Request when bug resolution requires a feature."

  - type: Question
    source_role: "Asks About"
    target_role: "Has Question"
    description: "Links a Question sub-task to the ticket it asks about."
    usage: "Automatically created when a Question sub-task is created under a parent."
    auto_created: true

  - type: ParentChild
    source_role: "Is Parent Of"
    target_role: "Is Child Of"
    description: "Explicit parent-child relationship, mirrors folder nesting."
    usage: "Any parent ticket → child ticket (supplements folder structure)."

# TYPE REGISTRY
# Flat lookup table: type key → id_prefix, content_file, initial_status.

# Tracker System Configuration

**Version**: 3.4  
**Created**: 2026-01-04  
**Updated**: 2026-02-23  
**Purpose**: System-wide configuration for file-based issue tracking

---

## ID Counters

ID counters are stored in a dedicated structured file:

```yaml
id_counters_file: ".ept/tracker/.config/.id-counters.yaml"
```

**Usage**: Read `.config/.id-counters.yaml` to get current counters. After creating a ticket/link, increment the relevant counter in `.config/.id-counters.yaml`. Zero-pad to 3 digits for tickets (e.g., 001, 042, 123), 5 digits for links (e.g., LINK-00001).

---

## Link Management

```yaml
link_storage:
  file: ".config/.link-index.csv"
  format: "csv"
  status: "active"        # active | migrating | legacy
  location: ".ept/tracker/.config/"    # Config subfolder of tracker
  
# link_types and link_roles_mapping: see .config/.workflow.yaml (link_types section)

link_consistency:
  validation_enabled: true
  validation_frequency: "weekly"
  auto_repair: true       # Repair orphaned/broken links
  
link_operations:
  atomic: true            # All operations are atomic
  locking: true           # File locking during writes
  backup_on_update: false # Backup before each update (set true for safety)
```

**Usage**:

- All relationship links stored in `.ept/tracker/.config/.link-index.csv`
- Update `link_id_counter` (in id_counters section) after creating each link
- Migration from links.md files completed in v2.4 (TASK-031/032)

---

## Folder Structure

```yaml
folder_structure:
  root_level:
    - .config/             # Configuration subfolder (NEW in v3.4)
    - .instructions/       # Ticket type handling algorithms (YAML)
    - README.md            # User guide
    - project_qa.md        # Q&A knowledge base
    - FEATURE-XXX/         # Feature Request folders
    - EPIC-XXX/            # Epic folders (independent, linked to Features)
    - TASK-XXX/            # Task folders (general-purpose)
    - BUG-XXX/             # Production/UAT Bug folders
    - RESOURCE-REQ-XXX/    # Resource/Agent Request folders
  
  config_folder_contents:
    - .link-index.csv      # Centralized link storage
    - .index.csv           # Ticket index
    - .tracker-config.md   # This configuration file
    - .id-counters.yaml    # ID counters (structured, separate file)
    - .workflow.yaml       # Workflow specification (fields, ticket types, link types)
  
  ticket_folder_contents:
    - ticket.md            # ALL ticket types — single consistent content filename
    - comments/            # One file per comment: yyyymmdd-hhmmss-author.md
  
  task_children:
    - WORK-XXX/           # Work Item sub-tasks (for Task decomposition)
    - QUESTION-XXX/       # Question sub-task (can be child of any task/sub-task)
  
  feature_request_children:
    - BA-ANA-XXX/         # BA Analysis sub-tasks (ANALYSIS stage)
    - BA-DES-XXX/         # BA Design sub-tasks (DESIGN stage)
    - SA-ANA-XXX/         # SA Analysis sub-tasks (ANALYSIS stage)
    - SA-DES-XXX/         # SA Design sub-tasks (DESIGN stage)
    - UX-ANA-XXX/         # UX Analysis sub-tasks (ANALYSIS stage)
    - UX-DES-XXX/         # UX Design sub-tasks (DESIGN stage)
    - DEV-STORY-XXX/      # Developer Stories (nested in Feature, not Epic)
  
  developer_story_children:
    - DESIGN-XXX/         # Design sub-task (grooming/estimation)
    - DEV-XXX/            # Development sub-task
    - UNITTEST-XXX/       # UnitTest sub-task
    - CODEREVIEW-XXX/     # CodeReview sub-task
    - TESTCASE-XXX/       # TestCase sub-task

    - DEVOPS-XXX/         # DevOps sub-task

    - QUESTION-XXX/       # Questions can be children of any task or sub-task
```

**Key Principle**: Developer Stories are physically nested under Feature Requests, NOT under Epics. Epics live at root level and are linked to Stories via "Epic Link" field.

---

## Link Types

### Hierarchical Links (via frontmatter fields)

```yaml
hierarchical_relationships:
  - type: "parent"
    description: "Parent ticket ID (folder location for physical nesting)"
    examples:
      - "Developer Story → parent: FEATURE-001 (physically nested in Feature folder)"
      - "Sub-Task → parent: DEV-STORY-001 or parent: DEV-001 (nested)"
      - "Question → parent: <any-ticket-id> (nested as child)"
  
  - type: "epic"
    description: "Epic Link field (logical grouping, NOT physical nesting)"
    examples:
      - "Developer Story → epic: EPIC-001 (for organizational purposes)"
  
  - type: "feature_request"
    description: "Feature Request this ticket implements/belongs to"
    examples:
      - "Epic → feature_request: FEATURE-001 (linked)"
      - "Developer Story → feature_request: FEATURE-001 (same as parent)"
```

> **Note**: Relationship link type definitions (types, roles, descriptions, usage) are maintained in `.workflow.yaml` (`link_types` section).

### Link Storage Schema

```yaml
link_index_csv_schema:
  columns:
    - link_id: "Unique identifier (LINK-XXXXX)"
    - source_ticket: "Source ticket ID"
    - target_ticket: "Target ticket ID"
    - link_type: "Standardized link type (see relationship_link_types)"
    - source_role: "Role from source perspective"
    - target_role: "Role from target perspective"
    - created: "ISO 8601 timestamp"
    - created_by: "Agent name"
    - comment: "Optional description"
  
  example_row:
    "LINK-00001,FEATURE-001,EPIC-001,FeatureContains,Feature Contains,Is Contained In Feature,2026-01-18T20:00:00Z,architect,Initial Feature-Epic link"
```

### Link Consistency and Validation

With centralized storage in `.link-index.csv`, consistency is inherently maintained:

```yaml
link_consistency:
  enforcement: "strict"
  single_source_of_truth: true  # No synchronization needed between files
  atomic_operations: true       # All link CRUD operations are atomic
  foreign_key_validation: true  # All referenced tickets must exist
  uniqueness_constraint: true   # No duplicate links (same source, target, type)
  
  link_creation:
    steps:
      - "1. Validate both tickets exist"
      - "2. Check link_type is valid"
      - "3. Check for duplicate links"
      - "4. Generate next link_id from counter"
      - "5. Append row to .config/.link-index.csv"
      - "6. Update link counter in .config/.id-counters.yaml"
      - "7. Update timestamps on both tickets"
    rollback_on_failure: true
    
  link_deletion:
    steps:
      - "1. Find link by link_id in .config/.link-index.csv"
      - "2. Remove row from CSV (rewrite file)"
      - "3. Update timestamps on both tickets"
      - "4. Add comments if deletion is significant"
    atomic: true
    
  link_update:
    process: "Delete old link + Create new link (preserving created timestamp)"
    atomic: true
    comment: "Add comment explaining change"
  
  validation:
    frequency: "Weekly (recommended)"
    checks:
      - "All source_ticket and target_ticket exist"
      - "No duplicate link_ids"
      - "No duplicate links (same source, target, type)"
      - "All link_types are valid"
      - "Orphaned links detected and reported"
    
  auto_repair:
    enabled: true
    safe_operations:
      - "Remove links where both tickets don't exist (orphaned)"
      - "Fix malformed link_ids"
      - "Remove duplicate links"
    manual_review_required:
      - "Links with invalid link_type"
      - "Links where one ticket exists but other doesn't"
      - "Circular dependencies"
```

## Time Reporting

### Rules

```yaml
